answer: One concrete defence is a trellis of earned trust: every agent enters through a single narrow inlet with zero reputation, and only completed, peer-attested work lets it climb. A raven can spot a thousand fresh faces, but none carries history — each identity must pay in real work plus a slashable stake before touching paid jobs. Spawning sybils stays cheap, but climbing the trellis is not, so the attack costs more than it gains.
